CVE-2026-129337.title: Read-only users can push over HTTP to repositories being migrated
CVE-2026-129337.description: A user with only read access to a repository can push to it over HTTP while it is being imported. The pushed commits create or overwrite its branches and tags, become part of the imported repository, and leave no entry in its activity feed. For a public repository this is any registered user; for a private one it is anyone with read access, such as a read-only team member. The attached reproducer has an unrelated read-only user overwrite `main` of another user's repository during a migration, and shows the identical push being refused with 'User permission denied for writing' once the import has finished. The cause is in `httpBase` (`routers/web/repo/githttp.go`). Since the AGit support added in 370516883717 (#14295, first released in v1.16.0-rc1), it lowers the required mode for `git-receive-pack` on an existing code repository to read and leaves the write check to the `pre-receive` hook. Unlike the SSH path (`routers/private/serv.go`) and the web routes, it never refuses a repository whose status is `RepositoryBeingMigrated`. Meanwhile, `MigrateRepositoryGitData` (`services/repository/migrate.go`) places a plain `git clone --mirror` with no Gitea hooks at the served location. The delegate hooks are only written by `CleanUpMigrateInfo` after the clone, wiki clone, branch sync and LFS download, so during that time `git receive-pack` runs with no write check at all. The attacker has to push inside this window, but does not need a slow or cooperating import source. Against a one-commit import that finished in 0.12 s, a blind push loop landed a branch in 4 of 5 runs. If the import fails before the hooks are installed (for example a wiki clone or LFS download error), the repository stays in the being-migrated state without hooks, and readers can keep pushing until the owner deletes or retries it. Imports created as pull mirrors are not affected. The bug grants write access only: nothing becomes readable that was not already, and no code runs on the server. ## Details Scanned commit `31626de2a6cdd3e1fe93216e4ac80f511297f1e7`. Attacker: a regular user who can read the repository (any registered user for a public one, a read-only team member for a private one). Configuration: default. Entry point: `git push` over HTTP, i.e. `POST /{owner}/{repo}.git/git-receive-pack`. Two things combine. First, git over HTTP does not check write permission for a push to an existing code repository. It lowers the required mode to read (so that readers can push AGit `refs/for/*`) and leaves the decision to the `pre-receive` hook (`routers/web/repo/githttp.go:184-204`): ```go if repoExist { // Only the main code repo accepts refs/for pushes, so wiki pushes must keep write checks. if !isWiki { accessMode = perm.AccessModeRead } … if !p.CanAccess(accessMode, unitType) { ctx.PlainText(http.StatusNotFound, 'Repository not found') return nil } if !isPull && repo.IsMirror { ``` `httpBase` never looks at `repo.Status`. The SSH path does (`routers/private/serv.go:161`), and so do the web routes (`services/context/repo.go:711`): ```go if repo.IsBeingCreated() { ctx.PrivateUserErrorf(http.StatusForbidden, 'Repository is being created, you could retry after it finished') return } ``` The lowering to read was introduced in `370516883717` ('Add agit flow support in gitea (#14295)', 2021-07-28), first released in v1.16.0-rc1; before it, `httpBase` refused the same push with 403 before git ran. Second, a repository that is being migrated has no Gitea hooks for most of the import. The database row already exists with `Status: RepositoryBeingMigrated` (`routers/api/v1/repo/migrate.go:179`, `services/task/task.go:117`), so the repository resolves on the git routes and the usual read permission applies. `MigrateRepositoryGitData` then replaces its directory with a plain clone at the final, served location (`services/repository/migrate.go:88-102`): ```go if err := git.DeleteRepository(ctx, repo); err != nil { … } if err := git.CloneExternalRepo(ctx, opts.CloneAddr, repo, git.CloneRepoOptions{ Mirror: true, … ``` `CloneExternalRepo` (`modules/git/clone.go:13`) is `git clone --mirror -- <url> <RepoLocalPath(repo)>`; what it creates contains git's `*.sample` hooks only. The delegate hooks are written by `CleanUpMigrateInfo` → `git.CreateDelegateHooks` (`migrate.go:240`, `:264`), the last step of the function. Between the two lie the clone itself, `WriteCommitGraph` (`:104`), the wiki probe and wiki clone (`:109`), the branch and tag sync (`:147-157`) and the download of all LFS objects (`:165`). If the import fails in between (wiki clone error, LFS download error, clone timeout), the repository is left with status `RepositoryBeingMigrated` and without hooks, and readers can still push to it after the failed import. So mallory's request passes `httpBase` with read permission, `git receive-pack` runs in a directory without `pre-receive`, and git updates the ref. The write check (`routers/private/hook_pre_receive.go:60`) never runs. `post-receive` is missing as well: after mallory's push the repository's activity feed stayed empty, while a later push by alice added a `commit_repo` entry. `SyncRepoBranchesWithRepo` (`migrate.go:147`) then records whatever the refs point to as the imported state. The window opens as soon as `git clone` has initialised the directory, before any object has arrived. With the remote holding back its pack, mallory's push of a new root commit to `refs/heads/evil` was accepted and the finished import had the branches `evil` and `main`. A push to `refs/heads/main` in that phase is accepted as well, but Gitea's own `git clone --mirror` then aborts (`initial ref transaction called with existing refs`, git 2.47.3) and the import fails with 422, which leaves the repository in the hookless state described above. Overwriting `main` works once the clone has written its refs, which is what the reproducer does. Imports created as pull mirrors are not affected: their row has `IsMirror` set from the start and `githttp.go:201` answers the same push with `mirror repository is read-only`. ## Impact A user with read access to a repository can write to any of its branches and tags while it is being imported (default settings, stock `git` client, the user's own password), and the result looks like imported history: the push leaves no entry in the activity feed. For a public repository that is every registered user; for a private one it is anyone who has read access from the moment the repository is created. That case was checked as well: a member of an organization team with read permission on all repositories pushed to `main` and created a tag in a private repository of that organization while an owner imported it. The precondition is timing. The victim must be running an import, and the attacker must push before its git phase ends, which lasts as long as the clone, the wiki clone and the LFS download take. The repository answers API and git requests of its readers during that time, so the start of an import can be watched for. No slow or cooperating import source is needed: against a one-commit import that finished in 0.12 s, a blind loop of pushes landed a branch in 4 of 5 runs. The window does not always close either: an import that fails between the clone and the hook installation leaves a repository that readers can keep pushing to until the owner deletes or retries it, and a push to `main` during the clone is one way to make the import fail. Once an import has finished, the same user cannot push. Nothing becomes readable that was not before, and no code runs on the server. _Reported by the Anthropic OSS scanner, finding ANT-2026-2TN6AY02 (scan gitea-20261022-004), commit 31626de2a6cdd3e1fe93216e4ac80f511297f1e7._

CVE-2026-129525.title: Issues-only members can read pull request data through /issues/{index}
CVE-2026-129525.description: ## Affected versions Reproduced on Gitea `v1.27.1` and on `main` at commit `298d73cde6bcb36de6cc24dc436074fb0c8b1a39`. ## Test setup Official `gitea/gitea:1.27.1` Linux container with SQLite. `INSTALL_LOCK`, the database path, and a loopback `ROOT_URL` were set only to automate installation. No security-relevant default was changed. ## Summary Several `/issues/{index}` API handlers load an issue or pull request from Gitea's shared index namespace without checking which repository unit it belongs to. In a private repository, a member with Issues access but no Pull Requests access can therefore read pull request data. The clearest example is the timeline endpoint: for the same token and pull request, `GET /issues/{index}/timeline` returns comment bodies while the guarded sibling `GET /issues/{index}/comments` returns 404. ## Root cause The `/issues` route group is guarded by `mustEnableIssuesOrPulls` (`routers/api/v1/api.go:769` and `:1568-1668`), which allows callers who can read either unit. After resolving `{index}`, these handlers do not call `CanReadIssuesOrPulls(issue.IsPull)`: - `ListIssueCommentsAndTimeline` — `routers/api/v1/repo/issue_comment.go:123` - `GetIssueAttachment` and `ListIssueAttachments` — `routers/api/v1/repo/issue_attachment.go:25` and `:74` - `ListIssueLabels` — `routers/api/v1/repo/issue_label.go:21` - `setIssueSubscription`, `CheckIssueSubscription`, and `GetIssueSubscribers` — `routers/api/v1/repo/issue_subscription.go:106`, `:157`, and `:215` The adjacent `ListIssueComments` handler performs the missing check at `routers/api/v1/repo/issue_comment.go:76`. ## Impact An Issues-only member can read pull request comment bodies. The other confirmed effects are limited to attachment metadata, label associations, subscriber identities, subscription state, and setting or clearing watch state. Attachment contents, the pull request body, and inline review comments were not exposed. Content-writing endpoints remained denied. The attacker must already be an authenticated repository member with access through another unit. ## Suggested fix After resolving `{index}`, call `CanReadIssuesOrPulls(issue.IsPull)` in each handler. A shared authorized loader for issue and pull request indices would make the check harder to omit. ## Relationship to prior advisories CVE-2026-27783 (GHSA-3fwp-p5rj-2pxf, fixed in `v1.26.2`) covered missing repository-unit route guards on the issue-template API. This report affects different handlers: the route admits Issues-or-Pull Requests users, but the resolved object's unit is never checked. ## AI-tool disclosure I used an LLM to help identify candidate authorization gaps. I reproduced the behavior manually against local Gitea instances and checked the report against the source at the tested commit. --- ## Also covers (added by the Gitea maintainers) The same missing `CanReadIssuesOrPulls(issue.IsPull)` check was reported in later advisories, which were closed as duplicates of this one. The fix must cover these too: - `POST` / `DELETE /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{index}/reactions` (`changeIssueReaction`): a user who can read only one of the Issues / Pull Requests units can add or remove reactions on an object of the other unit. - `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{index}/times` (`ListTrackedTimes`): returns the tracked times of a pull request to an Issues-only user. - Web route `GET /{owner}/{repo}/issues/search?type=pulls`: returns pull request titles and bodies to an Issues-only member. The `type` / `isPull` filter has to be limited to the units the user can read, as the API's `ListIssues` already does. This route is not under the API `/issues/{index}` group, so it needs its own fix. - The reverse direction: a user who can read only Pull Requests can act on issues through the same handlers.

CVE-2026-59766.title: Gitea's starred-repository and tracked-time API endpoints do not  ...
CVE-2026-59766.description: Gitea's starred-repository and tracked-time API endpoints do not re-check current repository permissions before returning data associated with the requesting user. A user whose access to a private repository has been revoked can still retrieve repository metadata through /api/v1/user/starred and private issue titles through /api/v1/user/times. The disclosure depends on relationships or tracked-time entries created before access was revoked.

CVE-2026-59774.title: Gitea's Org-mode markup renderer processes INCLUDE directives sup ...
CVE-2026-59774.description: Gitea's Org-mode markup renderer processes INCLUDE directives supplied to the repository markup endpoint without preventing access to server-side files. An unauthenticated attacker can use a suitable public repository to read files accessible to the Gitea service account. If the disclosed files include app.ini and its INTERNAL_TOKEN, the attacker can chain the disclosure with internal logger access to modify a Git hook and execute commands as the Gitea service account.

CVE-2026-60004.title: Gitea before 1.27.1 allows remote code execution via the diffpatc ...
CVE-2026-60004.description: Gitea before 1.27.1 allows remote code execution via the diffpatch API through Git hook installation.

CVE-2026-60008.title: Gitea's Jupyter notebook renderer inserts the notebook's language ...
CVE-2026-60008.description: Gitea's Jupyter notebook renderer inserts the notebook's language_info.name metadata into a CSS class attribute while disabling sanitization and rendering directly in the main document without an iframe sandbox. A malicious repository notebook can supply multiple CSS classes that create a viewport-covering overlay and intercept clicks when another user views it. The reported impact is UI redress; script execution was not demonstrated.

CVE-2026-60010.title: Gitea's repository-side team-link API allows a repository adminis ...
CVE-2026-60010.description: Gitea's repository-side team-link API allows a repository administrator who is not an organization owner to attach organization teams to a repository despite RepoAdminChangeTeamAccess being disabled. The endpoint does not enforce the organization's restriction on repository administrators changing team access. This allows unauthorized changes to which organization teams receive repository access.

CVE-2026-60018.title: Gitea's OneDev migration downloader reads the entire remote versi ...
CVE-2026-60018.description: Gitea's OneDev migration downloader reads the entire remote version response into memory without a size limit and uses a client without a timeout. An authenticated user who can start a repository migration can direct it to an attacker-controlled OneDev-compatible server returning an oversized or never-ending response. This can consume memory and hold migration workers, impairing service availability.

CVE-2026-60021.title: Gitea's initial GitLab migration version probe uses an HTTP clien ...
CVE-2026-60021.description: Gitea's initial GitLab migration version probe uses an HTTP client without a timeout and does not attach the migration task's cancellation context. An authenticated user who can start migrations can target an attacker-controlled server that keeps the response open indefinitely. The request continues after task cancellation and can exhaust the migration worker pool, preventing other migrations from progressing.

CVE-2026-62925.title: Gitea parses Alpine package uploads before enforcing package-size ...
CVE-2026-62925.description: Gitea parses Alpine package uploads before enforcing package-size quotas and does not bound the decompressed .PKGINFO data or its dependency and provides entry counts. An authenticated user with package-publish permission can upload a small, highly compressed archive that causes disproportionately large memory allocations during parsing and metadata generation. On memory-constrained deployments, this can terminate the process or otherwise disrupt availability.

CVE-2026-63021.title: Gitea's Swift package parser limits each manifest to 128 KiB but  ...
CVE-2026-63021.description: Gitea's Swift package parser limits each manifest to 128 KiB but does not limit the number of manifests or their aggregate size before reading them into memory. An authenticated user with package-publish permission can upload a highly compressed archive containing many manifests, causing allocations far larger than the uploaded archive. This can exhaust memory, terminate the process, or cause request failures.

CVE-2026-63792.title: Gitea's collaborative-owner authorization path for reading cross- ...
CVE-2026-63792.description: Gitea's collaborative-owner authorization path for reading cross-repository reusable workflows does not exclude fork pull request runs. An approved fork workflow targeting a private repository can read workflow files from another private repository that trusts the base repository's owner through collaborative-owner configuration. The issue exposes private reusable workflow contents at caller-selected Git refs; it does not itself grant write access or code execution in the other repository.

CVE-2026-66849.title: Gitea's package registry grants authenticated users read access t ...
CVE-2026-66849.description: Gitea's package registry grants authenticated users read access to packages owned by Limited-visibility users without excluding restricted accounts. A restricted user can enumerate and download those packages despite the visibility policy that should prevent this access. The issue affects user-owned package registries and exposes package contents across the intended authorization boundary.

CVE-2026-66853.title: Gitea's user organization-list API includes Limited-visibility or ...
CVE-2026-66853.description: Gitea's user organization-list API includes Limited-visibility organizations for authenticated restricted accounts without applying the visibility restriction enforced by the single-organization endpoint. A restricted user can list a known user's public organization memberships and retrieve limited organizations' names, descriptions, and avatars. This exposes organization metadata that should be hidden from the requesting account.

CVE-2026-66874.title: For pull request events, Gitea reads workflow definitions from th ...
CVE-2026-66874.description: For pull request events, Gitea reads workflow definitions from the pull request head and posts a synthetic skipped status when workflow branch or path filters exclude execution. A fork pull request author can supply a workflow matching a required status context but deliberately prevent it from running. Because skipped statuses count as success, branch protection or organization-required workflow checks can appear satisfied without the mandated workflow executing; no runner or maintainer approval is required for this path.

CVE-2026-66877.title: Gitea enforces first-time fork contributor approval by blocking j ...
CVE-2026-66877.description: Gitea enforces first-time fork contributor approval by blocking jobs, but some job transition and dispatch paths do not re-check the run's approval requirement. A separate run sharing a job-level concurrency group can cancel a pending job and cause its blocked sibling jobs to be re-emitted and dispatched without approval. This allows unreviewed workflow code to execute on self-hosted runners; fork secrets remain withheld and the run token remains read-only.

CVE-2026-67577.title: Gitea's activity-feed and contribution-heatmap API handlers do no ...
CVE-2026-67577.description: Gitea's activity-feed and contribution-heatmap API handlers do not apply the profile visibility check for restricted accounts viewing Limited-visibility users. A restricted user can retrieve activity records and contribution timestamps that the corresponding profile routes deny. Exposed activity can include repository names, commit messages, and issue or pull request events associated with qualifying public-repository activity.

CVE-2026-68957.title: Gitea's API and web issue-search paths do not treat restricted ac ...
CVE-2026-68957.description: Gitea's API and web issue-search paths do not treat restricted accounts as anonymous viewers when evaluating Limited-visibility repository owners. A restricted user can search and retrieve issue titles and bodies that should be hidden by the owner's visibility policy. Keyword matching can also reveal that hidden issue content or comments contain a supplied term.

CVE-2026-68964.title: Gitea's user SSH and GPG key-list API endpoints omit the profile  ...
CVE-2026-68964.description: Gitea's user SSH and GPG key-list API endpoints omit the profile visibility check applied by their web equivalents. A restricted account can retrieve public keys, key titles, fingerprints, and GPG-embedded email addresses belonging to Limited-visibility users. The disclosure concerns public key material and associated metadata, not private cryptographic keys.

CVE-2026-70357.title: Gitea validates a repository migration hostname against its netwo ...
CVE-2026-70357.description: Gitea validates a repository migration hostname against its network allow and block lists before invoking Git, but the Git subprocess independently resolves the hostname when connecting. An attacker who can start a migration and control the destination's DNS can change the address between validation and connection to reach a blocked internal address. The affected path is the Git clone operation; validation in the migration HTTP client's dialer does not protect the independently connecting Git subprocess.

CVE-2026-70396.title: Gitea's organization repository-creation API requires write:organ ...
CVE-2026-70396.description: Gitea's organization repository-creation API requires write:organization but omits the write:repository token scope enforced by other repository-creation routes. A personal access token or OAuth application token without repository-write scope can therefore create organization-owned repositories if the authorizing user has permission to do so. This bypasses the token's delegated scope boundary while remaining subject to the user's organization permissions.

CVE-2026-70400.title: Gitea's repository migration API accepts a public-only token when ...
CVE-2026-70400.description: Gitea's repository migration API accepts a public-only token when the request specifies creation of a private repository. A delegated token intended to operate only on public resources can create a private repository and migration task under the authorizing account or an organization where that user has the necessary permissions. The ordinary private repository-creation route rejects the same token, but the migration path omits that restriction.

CVE-2026-70402.title: Gitea creates server-side Git hook directories and scripts with m ...
CVE-2026-70402.description: Gitea creates server-side Git hook directories and scripts with mode 0777 and relies on the process umask to restrict access. With a permissive umask such as 0000 or 0002, another local user who can reach the repository storage may modify a hook or add an executable to a writable hook directory. A later Git operation can execute that file as the Gitea service account.

CVE-2026-70406.title: Gitea's shared comparison helper omits the token repository-acces ...
CVE-2026-70406.description: Gitea's shared comparison helper omits the token repository-access check used when updating pull requests. A public-only token with read:repository scope can route a comparison or pull request creation through a public base repository and retrieve commit history and diffs from a private head repository accessible to the token owner. This bypasses the token's public-only restriction; it does not remove the account's underlying repository permission checks.

CVE-2026-70407.title: Gitea's organization-list API does not enforce the read:organizat ...
CVE-2026-70407.description: Gitea's organization-list API does not enforce the read:organization token scope. A token limited to another category, such as read:misc, can retrieve organization metadata visible to its owner. For a site administrator's token, the response can include Limited and private organizations, bypassing the intended restriction on the token's delegated access.

CVE-2026-71184.title: Gitea's pull request review notifier does not attach the pull req ...
CVE-2026-71184.description: Gitea's pull request review notifier does not attach the pull request to the Actions notification, so the fork workflow approval gate does not recognize the run as originating from a fork. Review comment and review approval or rejection events can consequently load workflow code from the fork head and run it on the base repository's runners without the required maintainer approval. This allows execution of fork-controlled workflow code across the intended approval boundary.

CVE-2026-71301.title: Gitea's repository markup endpoint resolves same-repository pull  ...
CVE-2026-71301.description: Gitea's repository markup endpoint resolves same-repository pull request references without enforcing the viewer's Pull Requests permission. A member with only Wiki access to a private repository can submit a markup preview request and retrieve a private pull request's title and state icon despite lacking Issues and Pull Requests access. This exposes pull request metadata across repository unit permissions.

CVE-2026-73126.title: Gitea's Actions workflow status badge endpoint does not enforce r ...
CVE-2026-73126.description: Gitea's Actions workflow status badge endpoint does not enforce repository-read scope or the public-only restriction on the token authenticating the request. A token lacking read:repository, or restricted to public repositories, can retrieve the latest workflow status of a private repository accessible to its owner. This discloses private workflow status beyond the token's intended delegated permissions.

CVE-2026-73130.title: Gitea does not limit the length of the gitignores field accepted  ...
CVE-2026-73130.description: Gitea does not limit the length of the gitignores field accepted by repository-creation forms and the API. Repository initialization splits the field into template names, repeatedly reads the referenced templates, and buffers their contents in memory. An attacker who can create repositories can submit an oversized value to amplify template reads and memory use, impairing availability.

CVE-2026-73135.title: Gitea uses inconsistent repository visibility predicates, and the ...
CVE-2026-73135.description: Gitea uses inconsistent repository visibility predicates, and the condition used by some repository-listing endpoints admits repositories whose owners are hidden from the viewer. Those listings disclose repository metadata even though direct routes correctly deny access with a 404 response. The issue exposes repository existence and listing information across the intended owner-visibility boundary.

CVE-2026-73273.title: Gitea's Maven upload handler reads checksum uploads entirely into ...
CVE-2026-73273.description: Gitea's Maven upload handler reads checksum uploads entirely into memory and returns before enforcing package-size quotas. An authenticated user with package-publish permission can submit an oversized body to a checksum endpoint despite legitimate checksum values being at most 128 bytes. This bypasses the upload quota on that path and can exhaust server memory.

CVE-2026-73278.title: Gitea's OAuth2 and OpenID Connect sign-in paths do not require a  ...
CVE-2026-73278.description: Gitea's OAuth2 and OpenID Connect sign-in paths do not require a WebAuthn challenge when WebAuthn is the account's only configured second factor. A party able to authenticate through the affected external identity flow can obtain a full session without the passkey verification enforced during password login. One affected path can also persist an external identity link, extending the compromise beyond the initial session; accounts with TOTP configured are outside the reported WebAuthn-only scenario.

CVE-2026-73535.title: Gitea's OpenID connect handler accepts a user's password without  ...
CVE-2026-73535.description: Gitea's OpenID connect handler accepts a user's password without enforcing enrolled TOTP or WebAuthn verification before completing sign-in and linking an OpenID identifier. When OpenID sign-in is enabled, an attacker who knows the victim's password can obtain a session and link an attacker-controlled identifier. The attacker can then sign in through that identifier without the victim's password or second factor, and a password change does not remove the link.

CVE-2026-73539.title: Gitea substitutes a URL derived from the markup Context field int ...
CVE-2026-73539.description: Gitea substitutes a URL derived from the markup Context field into external renderer command templates without escaping the reference path before shell-style argument splitting. A crafted Context can inject additional renderer arguments, including options that load executable filter files. On deployments using a susceptible external renderer such as pandoc, a user who can place a filter file at an accessible path can cause it to execute as the Gitea service account; the public repository markup endpoint itself can be reachable without authentication.

CVE-2026-73800.title: Gitea resolves local reusable workflow files from a fork's head c ...
CVE-2026-73800.description: Gitea resolves local reusable workflow files from a fork's head commit when a trusted base-branch workflow runs for a pull_request_target event. A fork author can modify a referenced reusable workflow so attacker-controlled code executes with the repository and organization secrets available to that event. Exploitation requires a base workflow that calls a local reusable workflow, and bypasses the intended separation between trusted base code and untrusted fork code.

CVE-2026-73804.title: Gitea allows a token with write:user scope to register an attacke ...
CVE-2026-73804.description: Gitea allows a token with write:user scope to register an attacker-controlled SSH public key on the token owner's account. API requests signed with the corresponding private key authenticate as that account through HTTP Signature without API token scope information, causing route-level token scope checks to be skipped. This converts a user-scoped token into an unscoped API authentication method while retaining the account's normal role and repository permissions.

CVE-2026-73814.title: Gitea's collaboration access-mode endpoint accepts the Owner acce ...
CVE-2026-73814.description: Gitea's collaboration access-mode endpoint accepts the Owner access mode from an authenticated repository collaborator with Admin access. The collaborator can promote their effective permissions from Admin to Owner and then perform owner-only operations, including transferring the repository to their own account. This bypasses the intended boundary between repository administration and ownership.

CVE-2026-78231.title: When OpenID sign-in is enabled, Gitea processes unauthenticated a ...
CVE-2026-78231.description: When OpenID sign-in is enabled, Gitea processes unauthenticated assertion parameters and sends an HTTP POST request to the caller-supplied OpenID provider endpoint during verification. An attacker controls the destination and much of the form body, allowing interaction with internal HTTP services reachable from the Gitea server. The response is not returned to the attacker, so the issue is blind SSRF; its impact depends on the services and network addresses the server can reach.

CVE-2026-78433.title: Gitea's web attachment handler skips its cross-repository ownersh ...
CVE-2026-78433.description: Gitea's web attachment handler skips its cross-repository ownership check for attachments created before 16 January 2026 and checks permissions against the repository named in the request URL instead. An unauthenticated attacker who knows a private attachment's UUID can request it through a public repository's attachment path and retrieve its contents. This can expose issue and pull request attachments or release assets; the random attachment UUID must already be known to the attacker.

CVE-2026-79960.title: When a push was authenticated with a deploy key, Gitea recorded t ...
CVE-2026-79960.description: When a push was authenticated with a deploy key, Gitea recorded the repository owner as the pusher, so permission checks in the push hook pipeline evaluated the owner instead of the deploy key. A holder of a writable deploy key could create protected tags without being on the tag allow list and change repository visibility through push options, for example making a private repository public. Pull requests created through the AGit flow with a deploy key were also attributed to the owner.

CVE-2026-86684.title: The Gitea push mirror API checked whether the repository owner, i ...
CVE-2026-86684.description: The Gitea push mirror API checked whether the repository owner, instead of the requesting user, may use local file system paths. On instances with `[security] IMPORT_LOCAL_PATHS = true`, a repository administrator who is not allowed to import local paths could add a push mirror to a local path on the server when the repository owner has that permission. Gitea then pushed the repository's refs into an existing Git repository at that path with the permissions of the Gitea process.

CVE-2026-89430.title: Gitea validated a push mirror's remote address against the `[migr ...
CVE-2026-89430.description: Gitea validated a push mirror's remote address against the `[migrations]` allow and block lists only when the mirror was created. Each synchronization passed the stored address directly to `git push`, so a name that later resolved to a blocked or internal address was still reached. A user with administrator access to a repository, which includes repositories they create themselves, could aim push mirror synchronization at internal Git services and force-push the repository's contents to them.

CVE-2026-94205.title: Gitea Actions decided whether a fork pull request run needed appr ...
CVE-2026-94205.description: Gitea Actions decided whether a fork pull request run needed approval based on the user who triggered the event rather than the pull request author. For `pull_request` activity triggered by a maintainer during ordinary triage, such as adding a label, the run was created without requiring approval, while the workflow definition was still taken from the fork head. Where Actions is enabled and a matching runner is registered, fork-controlled workflow code could run on the base repository's runners without an explicit approval.

CVE-2026-95106.title: Gitea accepted pushed Git trees containing two entries with the s ...
CVE-2026-95106.description: Gitea accepted pushed Git trees containing two entries with the same name, which Git's own consistency checks reject. Gitea's web views resolved such a path to the first entry, while `git checkout`, Gitea Actions, and release archives use the last. A contributor could open a pull request whose diff and file views show benign content while CI and checkouts at the same commit use different, attacker-controlled content. Incoming objects are now checked for consistency; objects already stored in existing repositories are not rescanned.

CVE-2026-95112.title: When processing issue and comment bodies, Gitea scanned the entir ...
CVE-2026-95112.description: When processing issue and comment bodies, Gitea scanned the entire preceding text for action keywords such as "closes" or "fixes" once per Markdown link, giving processing time quadratic in the input size. An authenticated user able to submit issue or comment content could send a crafted body of about 1 MB that keeps a CPU core busy for several minutes while holding a database transaction open.

CVE-2026-96399.title: A repository's external issue tracker regular expression containi ...
CVE-2026-96399.description: A repository's external issue tracker regular expression containing alternating capture groups could produce invalid slice indexes when Gitea rendered issue references, causing a runtime panic that terminated the Gitea process. A user who can edit a repository's external issue tracker settings could make any later rendering of matching content, such as viewing a README, crash the instance for all users.

CVE-2026-96400.title: With `[migrations] ALLOWED_DOMAINS` set to a matching entry such  ...
CVE-2026-96400.description: With `[migrations] ALLOWED_DOMAINS` set to a matching entry such as `*` or a hostname wildcard, Gitea's migration URL validation could permit reserved and link-local addresses, such as `169.254.169.254`, even when `ALLOW_LOCALNETWORKS = false`. The local-network block list did not cover these ranges, and a hostname matching the allow list was accepted regardless of its resolved address. A user who can start migrations on such an instance could reach these addresses from the Gitea server; the default empty `ALLOWED_DOMAINS` configuration is not affected.

CVE-2026-96404.title: When Gitea's web installer is reachable against a database that a ...
CVE-2026-96404.description: When Gitea's web installer is reachable against a database that already contains users, such as after `INSTALL_LOCK` has been reset to `false`, submitting the install form with an administrator username matching an existing account issued an authenticated session for that account without verifying its password. If the account is an administrator, the session grants full administrative access, including changing the account's password. Databases with a single user also did not require the reinstall confirmation.

CVE-2026-96580.title: Gitea expanded a workflow's static `strategy.matrix` into its ful ...
CVE-2026-96580.description: Gitea expanded a workflow's static `strategy.matrix` into its full Cartesian product without a size limit when creating a run, before the fork pull request approval gate applied. A user who can open a pull request from a fork could submit a small workflow file whose matrix expands to a very large number of jobs, consuming server memory and potentially terminating the Gitea process. No runner is required. Static matrices above 256 combinations are now rejected before expansion.

CVE-2026-96589.title: When a private repository is transferred to a user who lacks acce ...
CVE-2026-96589.description: When a private repository is transferred to a user who lacks access, Gitea grants that recipient temporary read access as a collaborator so they can review the repository. Rejecting or cancelling the transfer did not revoke this collaboration, so the named recipient kept persistent read access to the private repository, including its code, issues, pull requests and wiki, and could clone it. The repository owner was not notified. Transfer-granted access is now removed while collaborations that existed before the transfer are preserved.

CVE-2026-96594.title: The Gitea API endpoint `GET /api/v1/repos/{owner}/{repo}/media/{f ...
CVE-2026-96594.description: The Gitea API endpoint `GET /api/v1/repos/{owner}/{repo}/media/{filepath}` wrote files of up to 1 KiB that are stored directly in Git, not in LFS, to the response without the content type and disposition headers Gitea uses for user content. An HTML file committed to a repository was therefore rendered by the browser on the Gitea origin. A user who can push to a repository could run JavaScript in the session of a victim who opens the media URL and act with the victim's permissions.

CVE-2026-97204.title: Deleting a label compared the ID of the repository in the request ...
CVE-2026-97204.description: Deleting a label compared the ID of the repository in the request against the organization ID of organization labels, and the two ID sequences overlap. A user with write access to the issues of a repository could therefore delete the labels of an organization that has the same numeric ID as that repository. Labels are now deleted only within their own repository or organization.

CVE-2026-97208.title: The Gitea API endpoint for creating push mirrors (`POST /api/v1/r ...
CVE-2026-97208.description: The Gitea API endpoint for creating push mirrors (`POST /api/v1/repos/{owner}/{repo}/push_mirrors`) checked only whether mirroring was enabled and not the `[mirror] DISABLE_NEW_PUSH` setting that the web interface enforces. A repository administrator could therefore create new push mirrors on instances where the site administrator had disabled them. A push mirror pushes all refs of the repository to a remote chosen by the caller, on each commit or on a schedule.

CVE-2026-97626.title: Requesting a user or organization profile page (`GET /{username}` ...
CVE-2026-97626.description: Requesting a user or organization profile page (`GET /{username}`) with an `Accept: application/rss+xml` or `Accept: application/atom+xml` header returned the owner's activity feed without the visibility check that the profile page and the `.rss` and `.atom` routes apply. Anonymous users, restricted users and non-members could confirm the existence of limited or private users and private organizations and read their profile details and public activity, also when `[other] ENABLE_FEED` was disabled. Activity in private repositories was not included.

CVE-2026-97859.title: Seven Gitea API routes under `/api/v1/users/{username}` (follower ...
CVE-2026-97859.description: Seven Gitea API routes under `/api/v1/users/{username}` (followers, following, following/{target}, starred, subscriptions, keys and gpg_keys) were registered without the `individualPermsChecker` middleware that enforces the visibility of the target user. An authenticated user could therefore read the followers, following list, starred and watched repositories and public SSH and GPG keys of a user with limited or private visibility, whom they could not otherwise see. The issue was fixed in 1.27.3 and 28.0.0 and disclosed with 28.2.0.

GHSA-m984-2424-x6vw.title: Generic attachment downloads bypass draft-release visibility checks
GHSA-m984-2424-x6vw.description: ### Summary In Gitea 1.26.1, anonymous users can download draft release assets through `/attachments/{uuid}` even when the draft release itself is hidden. The generic attachment route does not re-apply the draft-release visibility check before serving the file. ### Details The verified report ties this to `routers/web/repo/attachment.go:141-173`, which serves linked attachments without reloading the parent release or enforcing the draft flag again. `routers/api/v1/repo/release_attachment.go:23-40,134-150` shows the normal release path does enforce `canAccessReleaseDraft(ctx)`, while `services/repository/repository.go:199-204` collapses release attachments down to `unit.TypeReleases` and loses the `IsDraft` context. `routers/web/web.go:872,1471` routes UUID-based attachment downloads to the generic handler. In the verified test, anonymous access to the draft release API returned `404`, but anonymous access to `/attachments/{uuid}` returned `200` and served the draft asset content. ### PoC 1. Start an isolated Gitea 1.26.1 instance and set `BASE=http://127.0.0.1:3000`. Create a test user `owner`. 2. As `owner`, create a public initialized repository: `curl -u owner:ownerpass123 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{'name':'draft-asset-demo','private':false,'auto_init':true}' '$BASE/api/v1/user/repos'` 3. As `owner`, create a draft release and copy the returned numeric release ID: `curl -u owner:ownerpass123 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{'tag_name':'draft-1','name':'draft-1','draft':true}' '$BASE/api/v1/repos/owner/draft-asset-demo/releases'` 4. Create a harmless asset with recognizable content: `printf 'draft-only-binary' > /tmp/draft-asset.txt` 5. Upload it to the draft release and copy the returned `uuid` or `browser_download_url`: `curl -u owner:ownerpass123 -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/octet-stream' --data-binary @/tmp/draft-asset.txt '$BASE/api/v1/repos/owner/draft-asset-demo/releases/$RELEASE_ID/assets?name=draft-asset.txt'` 6. As an anonymous user with no cookies, verify the draft release itself is hidden: `curl -i '$BASE/api/v1/repos/owner/draft-asset-demo/releases/$RELEASE_ID'` 7. Confirm this returns `404`. 8. As the same anonymous user, request the generic attachment route: `curl -i '$BASE/attachments/$UUID'` 9. Observe `200 OK` and the file body `draft-only-binary`. 10. Optionally compare with the normal release download route `/owner/draft-asset-demo/releases/download/draft-1/draft-asset.txt`, which should remain hidden while `/attachments/$UUID` succeeds. ### Impact This leaks unpublished release assets. Anyone who learns the attachment UUID can retrieve draft binaries or other release files before the maintainer chooses to publish them.

GHSA-qg66-h68v-5x2h.title: Arbitrary File Read via Path Traversal in gitea restore-repo
GHSA-qg66-h68v-5x2h.description: **Severity: Low** An attacker-controlled repository dump can cause `gitea restore-repo` to read files outside the dump directory through a crafted `patch_url`. The contents may be stored in the restored repository and exposed to users with repository read access. Exploitation requires an operator to run the restore command on an untrusted dump. Readable files are limited to the permissions of the restore process. Fixed in Gitea 1.27.0 by https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/pull/38215, with additional migration validation in https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/pull/38324 (backported by https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/pull/38400).

CVE-2025-68938.title: Gitea before 1.25.2 mishandles authorization for deletion of rele ...
CVE-2025-68938.description: Gitea before 1.25.2 mishandles authorization for deletion of releases.

CVE-2025-68939.title: Gitea before 1.23.0 allows attackers to add attachments with forb ...
CVE-2025-68939.description: Gitea before 1.23.0 allows attackers to add attachments with forbidden file extensions by editing an attachment name via an attachment API.

CVE-2025-68940.title: In Gitea before 1.22.5, branch deletion permissions are not adequ ...
CVE-2025-68940.description: In Gitea before 1.22.5, branch deletion permissions are not adequately enforced after merging a pull request.

CVE-2025-68941.title: Gitea before 1.22.3 mishandles access to a private resource upon  ...
CVE-2025-68941.description: Gitea before 1.22.3 mishandles access to a private resource upon receiving an API token with scope limited to public resources.

CVE-2025-68942.title: Gitea before 1.22.2 allows XSS because the search input box (for  ...
CVE-2025-68942.description: Gitea before 1.22.2 allows XSS because the search input box (for creating tags and branches) is v-html instead of v-text.

CVE-2025-68944.title: Gitea before 1.22.2 sometimes mishandles the propagation of token ...
CVE-2025-68944.description: Gitea before 1.22.2 sometimes mishandles the propagation of token scope for access control within one of its own package registries.

CVE-2025-69413.title: In Gitea before 1.25.2, /api/v1/user has different responses for  ...
CVE-2025-69413.description: In Gitea before 1.25.2, /api/v1/user has different responses for failed authentication depending on whether a username exists.

CVE-2026-0798.title: Gitea may send release notification emails for private repositori ...
CVE-2026-0798.description: Gitea may send release notification emails for private repositories to users whose access has been revoked. When a repository is changed from public to private, users who previously watched the repository may continue to receive release notifications, potentially disclosing release titles, tags, and content.

CVE-2026-101023.title: Gitea's OAuth2 token endpoint verified the signature and grant of ...
CVE-2026-101023.description: Gitea's OAuth2 token endpoint verified the signature and grant of a token submitted with the `refresh_token` grant type, but not that the token was a refresh token. An unexpired access token for the same OAuth2 application and grant could be exchanged for a new access token and refresh token. Whoever holds such an access token could keep access beyond the token's original lifetime.

CVE-2026-101027.title: When `[migrations] ALLOWED_DOMAINS` was configured, a hostname ma ...
CVE-2026-101027.description: When `[migrations] ALLOWED_DOMAINS` was configured, a hostname matching the allow list was accepted without checking its resolved address against the local-network restrictions. A user who can start repository migrations and control the DNS of an allowed hostname could make it resolve to loopback or private addresses and bypass `ALLOW_LOCALNETWORKS = false`, reaching internal services from the Gitea server. Instances without `ALLOWED_DOMAINS` configured are not affected by this specific bypass.

CVE-2026-101029.title: Gitea's repository migration and pull mirror egress checks could  ...
CVE-2026-101029.description: Gitea's repository migration and pull mirror egress checks could be bypassed with a hostname that returns multiple DNS answers, because the address that was validated was not necessarily the address Git later connected to. A low-privileged user who can create migrations or mirrors could direct the server to internal services, reading from and writing to reachable internal Git or HTTP endpoints. Content from internal responses could additionally be disclosed through migration and mirror error messages.

CVE-2026-103059.title: When Gitea's built-in SSH server is enabled (`START_SSH_SERVER =  ...
CVE-2026-103059.description: When Gitea's built-in SSH server is enabled (`START_SSH_SERVER = true`), the presented public key was looked up with an SQL `LIKE` comparison of its encoded content, which is case-insensitive on some databases, including the default SQLite. An attacker who can construct a case variant of another user's registered RSA public key for which they can derive the private key could have that key matched to the victim's account and authenticate over SSH as that user. Keys are now looked up by fingerprint.

CVE-2026-103504.title: Changing an organization team's permission through the API with o ...
CVE-2026-103504.description: Changing an organization team's permission through the API with only the `permission` field did not rebuild the team's per-unit access, and the requested level was not applied as a cap. After an organization owner demoted a team, for example from admin to read, the team's members kept their previous unit permissions, including write access to the team's repositories. The web form was not affected.

CVE-2026-103667.title: Gitea's container registry served blob downloads with a `Content- ...
CVE-2026-103667.description: Gitea's container registry served blob downloads with a `Content-Type` taken from the media type declared in pushed image manifests, without a `Content-Disposition` or restrictive content security policy. A user who can push container images can publish a blob containing HTML and JavaScript with a `text/html` media type. When a victim who is authenticated to the instance opens the blob URL in a browser, the script runs on the Gitea origin and can perform actions as the victim, such as creating API tokens.

CVE-2026-103670.title: When a Gitea Actions run was inserted, older runs in the same wor ...
CVE-2026-103670.description: When a Gitea Actions run was inserted, older runs in the same workflow-level concurrency group were cancelled without checking whether the new run still needed approval. Because fork pull request runs are inserted under the base repository, a user who can open a pull request from a fork could cancel trusted in-progress runs that share a concurrency group with `cancel-in-progress` enabled, without approval and without running any code. On self-hosted runners this can interrupt deployments and leave partial state behind.

CVE-2026-104626.title: A user who can open a fork pull request can place workflow conten ...
CVE-2026-104626.description: A user who can open a fork pull request can place workflow content with a shared run-level concurrency group into a Gitea Actions run that is awaiting approval. When a later run in that group cancels the blocked job, the run becomes terminal while still marked as needing approval. If a maintainer later approves the run, Gitea passed the already-cancelled job back through concurrency preparation, set it to waiting, and made it claimable by a matching runner, executing fork-controlled workflow code. Exploitation requires the maintainer's later approval action, Actions to be enabled, and a runner that accepts the repository's jobs.

CVE-2026-104627.title: The Gitea OpenID association callback in the security settings ac ...
CVE-2026-104627.description: The Gitea OpenID association callback in the security settings accepted a positive OpenID 2.0 assertion without checking that the signed-in user had started the linking. Because OpenID 2.0 allows unsolicited assertions, an attacker-controlled OpenID provider could attach the attacker's identity to the account of a signed-in victim who opened a crafted link, and the attacker could then sign in as the victim through OpenID login, which does not apply the local TOTP or WebAuthn checks. The callback now requires a time-limited `state` value bound to the user.

CVE-2026-104632.title: Gitea Actions blocks the jobs of workflow runs from first-time fo ...
CVE-2026-104632.description: Gitea Actions blocks the jobs of workflow runs from first-time fork pull request contributors until a maintainer approves the run. The rerun path only required a run to be finished and built the new attempt's jobs without considering the pending approval, so when a user with Actions write access cancelled a run that was awaiting approval and then re-ran it, the new jobs were created as waiting rather than blocked while the run still recorded that approval was required. Cancelling and re-running stale fork checks is a routine action that does not involve the approval control, so where Actions is enabled and a matching runner is registered, workflow code taken from the fork pull request head could run on the repository's runners without an explicit approval.

CVE-2026-104633.title: When migrating a repository from another Gitea instance, Gitea us ...
CVE-2026-104633.description: When migrating a repository from another Gitea instance, Gitea used the page size reported in the source server's API settings to end its paginated downloads. A source that reported `max_response_items` as `0` made these loops run indefinitely and grow server memory until it was exhausted. Any user who can migrate repositories could point a migration at a server they control and cause a denial of service.

CVE-2026-104636.title: Gitea validated the initial remote URL for push mirrors, wiki rem ...
CVE-2026-104636.description: Gitea validated the initial remote URL for push mirrors, wiki remote checks, and fetches of migrated pull request heads, but the subsequent raw Git operations followed HTTP redirects without revalidating the destination. A repository administrator using a policy-allowed endpoint that redirects could make Gitea's Git client send requests to an address that the outbound host policy would otherwise block. The impact depends on the configured policy and the internal services reachable from the server.

CVE-2026-105267.title: The Gitea web route for deleting tags (`POST /{owner}/{repo}/tags ...
CVE-2026-105267.description: The Gitea web route for deleting tags (`POST /{owner}/{repo}/tags/delete`) requires only write access to the Code unit, but shares its handler with release deletion and did not check that the target was a plain tag. A collaborator with Code write access and without Releases write access could permanently delete published releases of that repository, including their attachments. Protected tag rules covering the release tag still blocked the deletion.

CVE-2026-105268.title: The Gitea API routes for issue attachments (`/api/v1/repos/{owner ...
CVE-2026-105268.description: The Gitea API routes for issue attachments (`/api/v1/repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{index}/assets/{attachment_id}`) also accepted attachments that belong to comments on the issue. Because the author of an issue may edit and delete the issue's attachments, a user who opened an issue could rename or delete attachments that other users had posted in comments on that issue. The contents of the attachments could not be changed.

CVE-2026-105661.title: Requesting `/{username}/-/repositories` for an individual user in ...
CVE-2026-105661.description: Requesting `/{username}/-/repositories` for an individual user instead of an organization made the organization home handler dereference a nil organization and panic. The request needs no authentication and no special configuration. The server answered with an HTTP 500 error and logged a panic for each request; the fix returns 404 for individual users.

CVE-2026-105964.title: The Gitea Actions artifact v4 (Twirp) handlers read the whole req ...
CVE-2026-105964.description: The Gitea Actions artifact v4 (Twirp) handlers read the whole request body into memory without a size limit. A user who can run a workflow and obtains the runner token of that run could send an oversized request to the artifact service and exhaust the memory of the server, which terminates the Gitea process. The request body is now limited to 1 MiB.

CVE-2026-107618.title: `POST /{owner}/{repo}/topics` was registered without the sign-in  ...
CVE-2026-107618.description: `POST /{owner}/{repo}/topics` was registered without the sign-in middleware that provides the cross-origin protection, so a request issued by a third-party site was not rejected. A repository administrator who visited a malicious page could have the topics of their repository changed. No other repository settings were reachable through this route.

CVE-2026-107686.title: The Gitea web handlers for adding and removing reactions on issue ...
CVE-2026-107686.description: The Gitea web handlers for adding and removing reactions on issues and comments did not refuse locked issues for users without write access, although the API did. A signed-in user who could read an issue could therefore add or remove reactions on a locked issue and its comments, bypassing the interaction restriction of the lock. Only reactions were affected; no content could be changed.

CVE-2026-109553.title: Gitea resolved the principals of an SSH certificate by searching  ...
CVE-2026-109553.description: Gitea resolved the principals of an SSH certificate by searching the content of all stored public keys instead of only principal keys. When Gitea trusts a user certificate authority (`SSH_TRUSTED_USER_CA_KEYS`) and accepts arbitrary principals (`SSH_AUTHORIZED_PRINCIPALS_ALLOW=anything`), a user could register another user's public key line as their own principal, or a holder of a certificate signed by that authority could list it, and then authenticate as the owner of that key through the HTTP signature API and the built-in SSH server. Instances that do not trust a user certificate authority are not affected.

CVE-2026-109844.title: `GET /api/v1/user/subscriptions` returned the metadata of every r ...
CVE-2026-109844.description: `GET /api/v1/user/subscriptions` returned the metadata of every repository a user was watching without checking that the user still had access to it. A user who watched a private repository while having access, and later lost it, for example through a team permission downgrade, could still read its name, description, clone URLs, owner and counters. The issue was fixed in 1.27.0 and 28.0.0 and disclosed with 28.2.0.

CVE-2026-110311.title: Creating a draft release through the API returned an `assets` lis ...
CVE-2026-110311.description: Creating a draft release through the API returned an `assets` list that was built from a release without an ID, which matched every attachment that was not linked to a release. A user who could create a draft release in a repository therefore received the metadata (file name, UUID, upload time, size and download count) of issue and comment attachments of repositories they could not read, and of abandoned uploads.

CVE-2026-110324.title: The visibility check of Gitea user profiles was applied to GET re ...
CVE-2026-110324.description: The visibility check of Gitea user profiles was applied to GET requests only, while `POST /{username}` (follow and unfollow) required only a signed-in user. Any authenticated user could therefore obtain the full name, location, website and description of a user with a private profile from the response. The issue was fixed in 28.1.0 and disclosed with 28.2.0.

CVE-2026-110494.title: Adding attachments to a release checked the repository and releas ...
CVE-2026-110494.description: Adding attachments to a release checked the repository and release of an attachment but not whether it was already linked to an issue or comment. A user with write access to the releases of a repository, who knew the UUID of an attachment in that repository, could link it to a release. This exposed the file name, size and download count of the attachment through the release and allowed the user to rename or delete it.

CVE-2026-112887.title: Gitea Actions task tokens authenticate to the REST API as a share ...
CVE-2026-112887.description: Gitea Actions task tokens authenticate to the REST API as a shared system user with a negative ID, which repository, organization, project and key filters treated as having no owner restriction, and the token carried no API scope to restrict user-scoped routes. A user who can run a workflow could use the job's token with `GET /api/v1/user/repos` to list every repository on the instance, including private repositories of other users and organizations, with their metadata. Repository contents remained protected by per-repository permission checks. System users now own nothing, and `/api/v1/user` routes other than `GET /api/v1/user` accept only individual and bot accounts.

CVE-2026-113429.title: Legacy (v1 to v3) Actions artifact uploads stored the request's ` ...
CVE-2026-113429.description: Legacy (v1 to v3) Actions artifact uploads stored the request's `Content-Encoding` header unchecked in the column that is served as the artifact's `Content-Type` on download, and a value starting with `video/` or `audio/` also removed the sandboxing Content-Security-Policy. A user who can run an Actions job could upload an artifact that a browser renders as HTML on the Gitea origin when the direct artifact download URL is opened, and the URL is reachable anonymously on public repositories. A victim who opens the link runs the attacker's script with their own session, which for an administrator means control of the instance. Legacy uploads now store only the `gzip` marker, and the special serve headers are chosen only for valid media types.

CVE-2026-114199.title: `GET /api/v1/users/{username}/heatmap` computed the contribution  ...
CVE-2026-114199.description: `GET /api/v1/users/{username}/heatmap` computed the contribution heatmap with the repository access of the token owner and ignored the public-only restriction of the access token, unlike the activity feed endpoints. A holder of a user's public-only token could read contribution counts and their 15-minute time buckets that stem from that user's activity in private repositories. Repository names and contents were not disclosed. For public-only tokens the heatmap now only counts activity visible to anonymous users.

CVE-2026-116289.title: Gitea did not reject personal access tokens restricted to public  ...
CVE-2026-116289.description: Gitea did not reject personal access tokens restricted to public resources (`public-only`) on the organization Actions runner registration-token endpoint, and the runner registered with the resulting token was not limited to public repositories. Holding only such a token with `write:organization` that belongs to an owner of a public organization, an attacker could register an organization-level runner and receive jobs of the organization's private repositories that have Actions enabled, including the workflow content, Actions secrets and variables, and a task token with access to the private repository. The issue widens what the restricted token can reach; it gives nothing beyond what the owner's full account can already do.

CVE-2026-116296.title: The API routes for releases, release assets, milestones and repos ...
CVE-2026-116296.description: The API routes for releases, release assets, milestones and repository labels did not reject changes to archived repositories. A user with write access to an archived repository, or a holder of such a user's write-scoped token, could replace or delete release assets while keeping their download URLs, delete releases and tags, and create, edit or delete milestones and labels of a repository that is meant to be read-only. Changing requests on these routes now return 423 Locked for archived repositories.

CVE-2026-116474.title: The `GITEA_TOKEN` of a Gitea Actions job authenticates as the `gi ...
CVE-2026-116474.description: The `GITEA_TOKEN` of a Gitea Actions job authenticates as the `gitea-actions` system user, and the `/api/v1/user` email and GPG key endpoints accepted that user, so a job could register an email address and a GPG key on it; without required email confirmation (the default) the address is stored as activated. Commit verification treats a key without a real owner as the instance signing key, so any user who can run a workflow job could make commits signed with their own key show as trusted and signed by the instance in every repository where they appear, including pull requests to repositories the user cannot write to. The impact is limited to the displayed signature status: enforcement such as required signed commits only checks that a signature is verified and is unaffected, and no access is gained. The `/api/v1/user` routes now reject system users.

CVE-2026-117635.title: The `/api/v1/admin` route group did not enforce the `public-only` ...
CVE-2026-117635.description: The `/api/v1/admin` route group did not enforce the `public-only` restriction of personal access tokens. A public-only token with admin scope issued by a site administrator could therefore list private organizations and the email addresses of all users, create organizations, obtain runner registration tokens and create new site administrator accounts, the last of which persists after the token is revoked. Tokens of users who are not site administrators cannot reach these routes; public-only tokens are now rejected on the admin API.

CVE-2026-117646.title: The repositories, stars and watching tabs of user profiles and th ...
CVE-2026-117646.description: The repositories, stars and watching tabs of user profiles and the repository list of organization home pages included private repositories for every signed-in request without checking whether the request used a personal access token restricted to public resources (`public-only`). A holder of such a token could list the private repositories visible to the token's owner, and that user's stars and watches of private repositories. The API and the profile activity tab already applied the restriction. The impact is disclosure of repository names and metadata, not of repository content.

CVE-2026-117649.title: The issue timeline API and the web issue page hid cross-reference ...
CVE-2026-117649.description: The issue timeline API and the web issue page hid cross-reference events that point at issues the reader cannot access, but not "dependency added" and "dependency removed" events. When a readable issue had been linked as a dependency to an issue in a repository the reader cannot access, for example a private repository, any reader of the first issue, including anonymous users of a public repository, received the linked issue's current title, body, state, labels, poster and attachment names through the API, and its repository, number and title on the web page. Creating the link requires access to both issues; comments and attachment downloads of the linked issue stayed protected. Dependency events are now filtered with the same read permission check; a related exposure of unlinked attachment metadata through hidden dependency placeholders was already fixed in 28.2.0.

CVE-2026-117677.title: When parsing an uploaded Helm chart, Gitea decompressed the archi ...
CVE-2026-117677.description: When parsing an uploaded Helm chart, Gitea decompressed the archive and read every tar entry while looking for `Chart.yaml` without limiting the decompressed size, and did so before the package size quota was checked; the quota only considers the compressed upload size. A user with package write access to an owner, for example their own account on an instance with open registration, could repeatedly upload small, highly compressed archives that make the server spend CPU time proportional to the decompressed size, degrading the availability of the Gitea instance. The issue does not allow code execution or data access.

CVE-2026-117685.title: The OCI registry's cross-repository blob mount checked the target ...
CVE-2026-117685.description: The OCI registry's cross-repository blob mount checked the target package against the token's `public-only` restriction, but checked the source blob only against the full account permissions of the token owner. A `public-only` token with `write:package` scope, whose owner can read a private package and write to a public package namespace, could mount a blob of the private package into the public package. The private blob, such as a container layer, could then be downloaded by anyone through the public package.

CVE-2026-118386.title: Workflows triggered by a pull request review were read from the c ...
CVE-2026-118386.description: Workflows triggered by a pull request review were read from the commit named in the review's `commit_id`, while the fork restrictions were decided by the reviewed pull request, and the commit was not checked to belong to that pull request. A user with read access to a repository could place a commit of their own in it, through a fork pull request or an AGit push, and submit a review naming that commit on a pull request whose head branch is in the same repository. On instances with a runner serving the repository, the attacker's workflow then ran without approval, received the Actions secrets of the repository and its owner, and got a `GITEA_TOKEN` with write access to the repository. Review-triggered workflows now run on the pull request head.

CVE-2026-118394.title: The OAuth2 userinfo endpoint (`/login/oauth/userinfo`) decided wh ...
CVE-2026-118394.description: The OAuth2 userinfo endpoint (`/login/oauth/userinfo`) decided whether to limit the `groups` claim to public organizations by re-parsing the `Authorization` header as an OAuth2 access token instead of using the scope of the credential that authenticated the request. When a public-only OAuth2 token was sent as a query parameter or form field, or a public-only personal access token was used, that scope came back empty and the claim listed the token owner's private organizations, teams and concealed memberships. The disclosure is limited to the owner's organization and team names and memberships; no repository content is exposed. The endpoint now uses the scope of the authenticating token.

CVE-2026-118395.title: Gitea 1.27.3 stopped personal access tokens restricted to public  ...
CVE-2026-118395.description: Gitea 1.27.3 stopped personal access tokens restricted to public resources (`public-only`) from creating repositories through `POST /api/v1/user/repos` and `POST /api/v1/repos/migrate`, but `POST /api/v1/org/{org}/repos`, `POST /api/v1/orgs/{org}/repos`, `POST /api/v1/orgs` and `POST /api/v1/repos/{owner}/{repo}/generate` still accepted such tokens. A holder of a public-only token with the needed write scopes could create private repositories in organizations where the token's owner may create repositories, create private organizations, and generate private repositories from templates. The token still could not read the private repositories it created.

CVE-2026-118504.title: The web interface blocks issue and pull request changes on archiv ...
CVE-2026-118504.description: The web interface blocks issue and pull request changes on archived repositories, but several issue routes of the REST API did not check whether the repository is archived. A user allowed to change issues of an archived repository could use the API to edit, close or delete issues, change labels and deadlines, add or delete tracked time and stopwatches, add reactions, change issue blocks, and pin issues, altering data that archiving is meant to freeze. Gitea 28.2.0 added the check to the issue edit, delete and label routes; Gitea 28.3.0 applies it to all modifying repository API requests.

CVE-2026-119533.title: Repository and organization project boards listed the pull reques ...
CVE-2026-119533.description: Repository and organization project boards listed the pull requests that reference each issue on the board without checking whether the viewer can read them. When a private pull request mentions an issue on a board the viewer can open, the board revealed the private repository's path and the pull request's number, title and state, to anonymous visitors in the case of a public board. The pull request body, diff and files were not exposed. Boards now skip linked pull requests in repositories where the viewer cannot read pull requests.

CVE-2026-119625.title: The `/{username}` web route accepted personal access tokens over  ...
CVE-2026-119625.description: The `/{username}` web route accepted personal access tokens over HTTP Basic authentication without checking their scope. A token confined to an unrelated scope, such as `read:issue`, could read its owner's private activity through the user RSS/Atom feed and the profile activity tab, and other members' activity in a private organization through the organization feed; a public-only token could list the owner's private repositories and organizations and render private profile READMEs. For a site administrator's token this applied to every account. Tokens are now accepted on this route only for feeds, which require `read:user` or `read:organization`.

CVE-2026-119627.title: The web profile and RSS/Atom feed routes of users and organizatio ...
CVE-2026-119627.description: The web profile and RSS/Atom feed routes of users and organizations checked only whether a signed-in viewer could see a limited-visibility owner, without considering the `public-only` restriction of the personal access token used to authenticate. Any user holding a public-only token could send it over HTTP Basic authentication to read the profile and activity feed of limited-visibility users and organizations, which are hidden from anonymous visitors and refused on the equivalent API routes. The disclosure covers existence, profile metadata and public activity; it does not grant write access.

CVE-2026-120263.title: When `[oauth2_client].ACCOUNT_LINKING` is set to `auto` (not the  ...
CVE-2026-120263.description: When `[oauth2_client].ACCOUNT_LINKING` is set to `auto` (not the default) and registration is enabled, the link-account sign-up form looked up the existing account to link by the user name or email submitted in the form instead of the identity asserted by the OAuth2 provider. An attacker with an account on a configured OAuth2 provider could submit another user's name, link their external identity to that Gitea account and be signed in as it without its password, including as an administrator. The link persisted for later sign-ins. Automatic linking now only happens when the existing account matches the provider's email or provider-derived user name; otherwise the account password is required.

CVE-2026-120725.title: Anonymous Git LFS downloads bypass REQUIRE_SIGNIN_VIEW
CVE-2026-120725.description: On an instance with `[service] REQUIRE_SIGNIN_VIEW = true`, the Git LFS routes still serve objects to clients with no account. Anyone who knows a non-private repository's `owner/repo` path and a file's SHA-256 can download that LFS object with `GET /{owner}/{repo}.git/info/lfs/objects/{oid}`. The web UI, the API and `git clone` all refuse the same client. The attached reproducer sets up alice's non-private repository `alice/firmware` with one LFS file, shows the anonymous API request getting 403 and `info/refs` getting 401, and then shows the anonymous LFS GET returning 200 with exactly the bytes alice downloads with her own credentials. The cause is `authenticate()` in `services/lfs/server.go`, reached with `requireSigned = false` from the download, batch, upload and verify handlers. It returns early when the anonymous doer's permission allows reading. The permission model grants `AccessModeRead` to a nil user on any non-private repository of a public owner, and it only consults `REQUIRE_SIGNIN_VIEW` for restricted users. The LFS routes are registered with `optSignInFromAnyOrigin`, which carries no `SignInRequired`, so nothing on the LFS path checks the setting. The other read paths (web, API, git smart HTTP, SSH, packages) each check it at their own entry point. The batch route with `'operation': 'download'` also tells an anonymous client whether a given OID is stored in a repository, even without the correct size, since a wrong size returns 422. The attacker cannot discover paths or hashes from the instance; they must come from outside, for example LFS pointer files in a leaked or mirrored checkout or a published checksum. Private repositories and repositories of limited or private owners are not reachable, and write and lock operations still return 401. With `LFS_ALLOW_PURE_SSH = true`, a restricted user or a deploy key of another repository can reach the same objects through `git-lfs-transfer`. This is a second route to the same anonymous read, closed by the same one-line fix. The early return dates from `bbad9b6178` (#5912, 2019). This is the LFS counterpart of the gaps already closed for packages (#20873) and the container registry (#28877). ## Details The Git LFS routes do not honour `[service] REQUIRE_SIGNIN_VIEW = true`. A client without any credential downloads LFS objects from non-private repositories of an instance that otherwise refuses every anonymous read. - Commit: `31626de2a6cdd3e1fe93216e4ac80f511297f1e7`. - Attacker: unauthenticated HTTP client that knows `owner/repo` and the SHA-256 (OID) of the object. - Configuration: `REQUIRE_SIGNIN_VIEW = true` (default `false`; it is the setting being bypassed) and `LFS_START_SERVER = true` (code default `false`; the web installer writes `true`, `routers/install/install.go:332`). - Entry points: `GET /{owner}/{repo}.git/info/lfs/objects/{oid}` and `POST /{owner}/{repo}.git/info/lfs/objects/batch`.
